name: MEXICO

flag.title: Flag of México
flag.note: Green, white & red with eagle emblem

lead: Mexico sits at the base of North America where snowy volcanoes loom over ancient pyramids and jungle hides jaguars. Home to the mighty Aztec Empire and a culture that turns remembering the dead into a joyful fiesta, Mexico gave the world chocolate, corn, and colour television.
geo: Mexico wears three faces: a spiny desert north, a towering mountain spine called the Sierra Madre, and thick tropical jungle in the south. Two great seas hug it on either side.
Mexico City sits 2,240 m above sea level — so high that visiting footballers struggle to breathe. The country also has 200 volcanoes, with 48 still active today.
animals: The golden eagle on Mexico's flag is real — a bird that can spot a rabbit two kilometres away. Gentle whale sharks cruise Yucatán's reefs, big enough to swim alongside.
The axolotl is a smiling, feathery-gilled salamander that never fully grows up and can regrow lost limbs. It lives only in Xochimilco's canals inside Mexico City.
culture: Every November, families build flower-covered altars and visit candlelit cemeteries to welcome ancestors' spirits for Día de los Muertos. It's joyful: marigolds, music, and favourite foods of loved ones.
Mariachi bands in silver-studded suits play trumpets and violins while street stalls sell tacos, tamales, and buttered corn. Mexican cuisine is a UNESCO world heritage.
history: Long before Europeans arrived, the Aztec Empire ruled from Tenochtitlan, a glittering island city where Mexico City stands today. At its peak the city held around 300,000 people trading gold and cacao.
Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés toppled the Aztecs in 1521. Priest Miguel Hidalgo rang his church bell in 1810 to spark revolt, and Mexico won independence in 1821.
wows: Cholula's pyramid is the world's biggest by volume — so wide a whole church sits on top.
Mexico's 1940 colour-TV patent later helped NASA beam back colour images of Jupiter.
Mexico City is sinking into the ancient lake beneath it — some spots have dropped over 12 m in a century.
The Chihuahua is the world's tiniest dog breed, named after a Mexican state bigger than the UK.
Every winter, hundreds of millions of monarch butterflies fly 4,500 km from Canada to Mexico's forests.
The Americas' first printing press was set up in Mexico City in 1539, centuries before most neighbours.
The Maya and Aztecs drank chocolate as a bitter spiced liquid long before anyone added sugar.

myths.fact: Rainforests, cloud forests, coral reefs, and fertile valleys cover far more of Mexico than its famous northern deserts.

myths.myth: Day of the Dead is Halloween
myths.fact: Día de los Muertos (1–2 Nov) is a warm family reunion with ancestors — marigolds and favourite foods, not frights.
